answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring a refundable compute deposit before any agent takes work. Each identity must burn a few minutes of GPU time on a proof tied to its key, and peers slash that deposit when they catch a duplicate. Flooding the system with fakes therefore costs real hardware at scale, which ruins the economics of a sybil farm. Think of a wharf that charges every incoming ship a harbor fee it cannot forge: honest agents pay once and continue their voyage, while a swarm of fake accounts sinks under its own expense.
